title: Cosine Is an Even Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Using the unit circle, decide whether f(x)=cos x is even, odd, or neither.

steps.title: Negate the Angle on the Unit Circle
steps.mathExpression: (\cos(-x),\sin(-x)) \text{ is the mirror of } (\cos x,\sin x)
steps.explanation: Reversing the angle reflects the circle point across the x-axis, which preserves the horizontal coordinate.
steps.why: The x-coordinate of the unit-circle point is the cosine value.

steps.title: Read Off the Identity
steps.explanation: Because the horizontal coordinate is untouched by the reflection, cosine of a negated angle equals cosine of the angle.
steps.why: Reflection across the x-axis changes only the vertical coordinate.

steps.title: Classify
steps.explanation: The identity holds for every real x, so cosine is an even function; its graph mirrors across the y-axis.
steps.why: Meeting the definition f(-x)=f(x) globally is exactly evenness.
